events.explanation: This window is the standout choice because it wins on both counts at once: at 22.12p/kWh it is the cheapest of all candidates and comfortably inside the 22.79p cap, and at 55gCO2/kWh it also ties for the lowest carbon intensity of the day. That happens because the midday solar peak pushes both wholesale prices and grid emissions down together, so there is no genuine price-versus-carbon sacrifice to make here. The only real trade-off is timing rather than cost: charging over 11:00-15:00 means the battery is full well before the evening, and it is effectively the last compliant slot -- the very next window (11:30) already jumps to 23.46p, breaching the cap, and prices then climb steeply towards 36p as solar fades into the evening peak. The overnight windows are the opposite bargain: they look conventionally 'off-peak' but are both dearer (23.75-26.84p, several above the cap) and roughly two to three times more carbon-intensive, because the grid is leaning on gas rather than sun. Charging midday and holding the energy for the evening peak therefore maximises both margin and emissions savings.

No other within-cap window matches both its price and carbon profile, so this is clearly the best trade-off available.
